title: The effect cue sheet (sound/sound_cues.json)
description: Every designed sound in a film: one cue per picture beat, one deliberate sound per kind of interaction, each able to be measured on its own. The effects engine writes it (gated on proof 3); a person can also write one for hand-made stems. `slate verify` reads it for cue sync (every anchor within a frame of its beat) and repeats. Times are film seconds; `t` is when the cue's own audio starts, `beat` is the picture moment it serves, and `anchor` says what the ear syncs to: onset (the first sample within 12 dB of the sound's peak), onset30 (paper: within 30 dB), peak20 / peak50 (the loudest 20 or 50 ms of air or a swell), end / end30 (where a lift or a drawn line finishes), none (beds). A gesture of overlapping notes lists them in `notes`, and each note is measured on its own.

palette.description: the brand whose palette made these cues

silences.description: planned silences (a held breath): effects stop dead

beds.description: planned continuous beds (plate audio), exempt from the drone check

t.description: film time the note's own audio starts

kind.description: the kind of interaction (tap, type, land, snap, count, draw, data, page, stamp, whoosh, swell, character, impact, or a brand's own)

sound.description: the one deliberate sound this kind uses (a material, the same for every cue of the kind)

event.description: the picture beat's id in timing/visual_events

file.description: the cue rendered on its own (film-relative or absolute)

params.description: what shapes the sound (pitch, cents, velocity, take, seed): its identity when there's no file
